items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I became acquainted with an Italian name Sergio Sangiorgi whom I later found out was a count and a lover of jazz.

ctx.x: One day, I received a letter from Lily saying that she was coming to Rome. As it was written in French, I could not read much of it, but I thought I understood what day and the hour she would arrive and I intended meeting her at the station. A few days later, I was coming from the American Express Company and happened to look into a taxi that had stopped and who should I see but Lily! I was surprised, because I had not been expecting her at that time. What happened was that I had mixed up the time of her arrival…

I became acquainted with an Italian name Sergio Sangiorgi whom I later found out was a count and a lover of jazz. I also became acquainted with a bass player named Carlo Loffredo who was president of the Hot Club of Rome and did a concert with the Roman New Orleans Jazz Band of which he was a member. This happened the 10th of April, and featured Arstella Whittier, Big "Boy" Goodie, Armando Travaioli without his big band and Ivan Vandor, a soprano sax man and member of the Roman New Orleans Jazz Band. Fred Palmer could speak the Italian language quite well and he made the acquaintance of an impressario who had nothing but ideas and this fellow told Fred that he was going to put on a show and wanted to use us. So we started rehearsing at Count Sangiorgi's home with a Martinque musician named Edouard Pajaniandy whom I had met in Paris.
